caption:
This morning: a backdoored Claude Code extension hit the Cursor Marketplace, with up to 5,000 developer systems impacted.

Three new data points: the bad version was live for about 11 hours. The malicious loader is just 66 lines. It was the third attack using the Claude name in a week.

My take: auto-update is a trust decision. Measure what your team installs and who approves it.

Comment CLAUDE and I will send you the details by DM.

Sources in the first comment.

scenes: This morning I covered the backdoored Claude Code extension on Cursor's marketplace, with 5,000 developer systems impacted. I went back in to check the numbers around it.
First, the bad version was live for about 11 hours, from 2:27 am to 1:35 pm Pacific, according to Cursor.
Second, the malicious loader is only 66 lines, pasted in front of the real extension code. Small change, big access.
Third, this was the third time in a week that attackers used the Claude name, after fake download pages and fake apps.
My take: Auto-update is a trust decision. Measure which extensions your team runs and who approves them, before an attacker does it for you.
